dedupe_keys.name: exposure of global rail and road infrastructure to future record breaking climate extremes cmip6

description: This study estimates how the exposure of global rail and road infrastructure to eight record-breaking meteorological hazards, including extreme temperature and precipitation, changes under CMIP6 climate projections. It finds that higher extreme heat and an increasing thaw-freezing index ratio are the greatest threats, with expected annual exposures 4 and 2 times the average of the eight hazards, and that the share of compound drought and heavy rain events rises from 7 to 18 percent as emissions grow. Peak exposure under SSP2-4.5 and SSP1-2.6 averages 29 and 52 percent lower than under SSP3-7.0, but most areas will still face multiple hazards. The authors are from Beijing Normal University, Oregon State University and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Coverage: global. Format and access: open access article in Earth's Future (2024). Licence and cost: CC BY-NC-ND, free. Caveats: exposure, not damage or vulnerability; data availability is not stated in the abstract record read. It supports hazard exposure and climate adaptation screening of transport networks. It relates to the global port multi-hazard risk data and OpenStreetMap in the catalogue.
